messages.author: 510ab88df6cfabe4
messages.subject: colext, Yearly-site-level covariates > contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels
parts:
I am attempting to test the effects of season on the movement of a desert species in a large camera grid- we have reason to believe that the species will shift habitat and location preference based on the season.

R=100 (cameras = sites)
J=50 (observation periods per season)
T=2 ( 2 seasons, Hot and Cold)

#phony observational data- to simulate Hot season and Cool season samples bound by colums ( i.e. cbind(hot, cool))
Hot<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.5),nrow=100,ncol=50)
Cool<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.25),nrow=100,ncol=50)
y<-cbind(Hot,Cool)

#Yearly-Site Covariates
#Based on the other threads in this forum I have ensured that the factor has 2 levels associated with it both "Hot" and "Cool" ( I know there is a more concise way to write this next step, but I am just ensuring that i haven't accidentally missed something)

h<-(matrix("Hot",100,1))
c<-(matrix("Cool",100,1))
h<-factor(h,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
c<-factor(c,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
season<-data.frame(h,c)

#Generate the unmarkedMultFrame:
umf2 <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=all,numPrimary=2,yearlySiteCovs = list(season=season))

Now you run a naive model, no problem;
fm <- colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf2)

but, if i run a model with Yearly site level covariates
fm.1<-colext(~1, ~1,gammaformula = ~season-1, ~1, umf2)

Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) : 
  contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels

Based on the threads in the forum and elsewhere, this has to do with the factor levels not being attributed properly, however- If i check my unmarkedMultframe:
 
#Summary:
100 sites
Maximum number of observations per site: 138 
Mean number of observations per site: 125.8 
Number of primary survey periods: 2 
Number of secondary survey periods: 69 
Sites with at least one detection: 24 

Tabulation of y observations:
    0     1  <NA> 
12505    75  1220 

Yearly-site-level covariates:
  season   
 Cool:100  
 Hot :100

and if i check the slot for Yearly-Site Covariates:
> class(umf2@yearlySiteCovs$season)
[1] "factor"
> levels(umf2@yearlySiteCovs$season)
[1] "Cool" "Hot"

So the levels ARE attributed to the factors. I can run other sample code from the vignette fine but cannot see any difference in my data structure.
I am at a loss and am out of ideas for how to address this issue, i am sure i have done something obvious wrong...Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] colext, Yearly-site-level covariates > contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels
parts:
Hi Chris,

There are only numPrimary-1 time intervals during which colonization and extinction occur, so with only 2 primary periods, there is only 1 time interval. 'unmarked' deals with this by ignoring the last column of each yearlySiteCov, which explains your error.

Richard

I am at a loss and am out of ideas for how to address this issue, i am sure i have done something obvious wrong...Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance.

Chris

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] colext, Yearly-site-level covariates > contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels
parts:
Hi all,

when you have just two primary periods, this gives one parameter for the dynamics rates: colonization and extinction. You may make these parameters site-specific and model them with site-covariates, but you can logically not model temporal variation in them, because there is none.

Best regards  --- Marc
From: unma...@googlegroups.com [unma...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Jeffrey Royle [jar...@gmail.com]
Sent: 17 April 2018 18:52
To: unma...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [unmarked] colext, Yearly-site-level covariates > contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels

Let me clarify this response: It doesn't make sense to model colonization as a function of season since there is only 1 interval over which colonization can occur (as Richard noted).  Likewise it doesn't make sense to use a dummy variable here either.


On Tue, Apr 17, 2018 at 12:44 PM, Jeffrey Royle <jar...@gmail.com> wrote:
hi all,

The season variable is constant within a season and since there is only one colonization event, that seems to be the case.  Indeed, it doesn't even make sense to model colonization as a function of season in this case.



On Tue, Apr 17, 2018 at 12:40 PM, Kate <kate.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
Sorry to ask a follow up question to this so long after the original post. Since unmarked ignores the last column of each yearlySitecov, does that mean we need to create a dummy column to get the code to work?


On Wednesday, October 5, 2016 at 2:16:52 AM UTC-6, Christopher Barichievy wrote:

Well I feel like an idiot! I should have noted that.

Thanks for the rapid response, much appreciated.

On Friday, 30 September 2016 13:39:09 UTC+2, Richard Chandler wrote:
Hi Chris,

There are only numPrimary-1 time intervals during which colonization and extinction occur, so with only 2 primary periods, there is only 1 time interval. 'unmarked' deals with this by ignoring the last column of each yearlySiteCov, which explains your error.

Richard
  

On Fri, Sep 30, 2016 at 5:51 AM, Christopher Barichievy <cbari...@gmail.com> wrote:
 I am attempting to test the effects of season on the movement of a desert species in a large camera grid- we have reason to believe that the species will shift habitat and location preference based on the season.

R=100 (cameras = sites)
J=50 (observation periods per season)
T=2 ( 2 seasons, Hot and Cold)

#phony observational data- to simulate Hot season and Cool season samples bound by colums ( i.e. cbind(hot, cool))
Hot<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.5),nrow=100,ncol=50)
Cool<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.25),nrow=100,ncol=50)
y<-cbind(Hot,Cool)

#Yearly-Site Covariates
#Based on the other threads in this forum I have ensured that the factor has 2 levels associated with it both "Hot" and "Cool" ( I know there is a more concise way to write this next step, but I am just ensuring that i haven't accidentally missed something)

h<-(matrix("Hot",100,1))
c<-(matrix("Cool",100,1))
h<-factor(h,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
c<-factor(c,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
season<-data.frame(h,c)

#Generate the unmarkedMultFrame:
umf2 <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=all,numPrimary=2,yearlySiteCovs = list(season=season))

Now you run a naive model, no problem;
fm <- colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf2)

but, if i run a model with Yearly site level covariates

Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) :

Based on the threads in the forum and elsewhere, this has to do with the factor levels not being attributed properly, however- If i check my unmarkedMultframe:
